chunks: Jarud said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I have daughters.' So he said: 'Perhaps you are wishing for their deaths. Know that if you wish for their deaths and they die, you will not be rewarded, and you will meet God, Mighty and Majestic, on the Day you encounter Him, while you are a disobedient one.'

key_terms.تَتَمَنَّى مَوْتَهُنَّ: Wishing for their deaths — the sinful attitude of desiring one's daughters to die out of dissatisfaction
key_terms.عَاصٍ: A disobedient one — one who transgresses God's command by wishing harm upon his daughters
key_terms.لَمْ تُؤْجَرْ: You will not be rewarded — denial of divine recompense for the one who harbors such a wish

ai.seo_question: Is it sinful to wish for the death of one's daughters in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) rebukes a companion who hinted at dissatisfaction with having daughters. The Imam warns that wishing for one's daughters' deaths is an act of disobedience against God, and that such a person will receive no spiritual reward even if the daughters die, and will face God on the Day of Judgment as a sinner. This hadith directly counters the pre-Islamic Arab attitude of considering daughters a burden or source of shame.
